The data behind the paper

A descriptive tour of every series used in “Whose Dates Do Prices Obey? Fiscal Regime Change and the Anchoring of Inflation” (Gustavo Vargas, 2026)

This page presents the data, not the results: what each series is, where it comes from, what window the paper uses and what the raw monthly rates look like, with the reform date marked. Every chart regenerates from the sources in this repository with python src/datos_descriptivos.py; the break tests and estimates live in src/estimacion/ and in the paper's appendix.

The census counts 34 stabilisations (1921–2025), of which 31 have usable monthly data — 46 monthly series in all, plus three daily series for the 2022 UK episode, a 19-country cross-section for the COVID inflation and two quarterly US velocity series. Hand-digitised series carry their source, page numbers, splices and known printing errata in the file headers under data/manual/; the rest load from public APIs without keys (FRED, IMF, and the central banks of Brazil, Peru and Argentina), cached under data/raw/.

The Table 1 sample: fifteen stabilisations with a fiscal anchor

The episodes behind the paper's main timing test: monthly price indices (and the broadest monthly money aggregate where one exists) around each fiscal reform.

The 2022 UK episode (daily data)

1 September to 31 October 2022: the pound (FRED DEXUSUK) and the ten-year nominal and real zero-coupon gilt yields (Bank of England IADB, IUDMNZC and IUDMRZC); n = 43 trading days. Dotted lines: the mini-budget (23 September), the Bank's intervention (28 September) and the U-turn (17 October).

US velocity series (1959–2025)

M2 velocity (FRED M2V) and the velocity of Divisia M4 — nominal GDP over the Center for Financial Stability's Divisia M4 — as plain levels. The paper's section 7 runs the stationarity battery on exactly these two series.
